body:
## Summary

The methods assume that all external controls are not treated. The setup functions do not make sure of this. If the data contains external patients with treatment `1`, `ec_ipw()` and `ec_aipw()` use them in different ways. If those patients really were treated, the result has bias.

## Steps to reproduce

```r
library(rdborrow)
d <- SyntheticData
d$A[d$S == 0][1:20] <- 1

setup_analysis_primary(
  data = d,
  trial_status_col_name = "S",
  treatment_col_name = "A",
  outcome_col_name = c("y1", "y2"),
  covariates_col_name = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"),
  method_weighting_obj = ec_ipw("S ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5")
)
```

## Expected result

The function stops with an error that tells the user that external controls must have treatment `0`.

## Actual result

The function accepts the data. Then:

- `ec_ipw()` uses the treated external patients as controls, because it selects external controls by trial status only.
- `ec_aipw()` does not use them in its outcome model, because that model selects on treatment `0`.

When the 20 patients really are treated, the estimate changes. In one adversarial review data set, the estimate changed from -1.16 to -3.22 at `weight = 1`.

## Cause

`setup_analysis_primary()` and `setup_analysis_OLE()` do not examine the treatment values of the external controls.

## Correction

In `setup_analysis_primary()` and `setup_analysis_OLE()`, stop with an error if a patient with trial status `0` has treatment `1`.

Add a test for this error.

## Affected functions

`setup_analysis_primary()`, `setup_analysis_OLE()`. The incorrect use occurs in `ec_ipw()` and `ec_aipw()`.

## Related

Found by two testers in the adversarial review pilot (#101).
title: Setup functions accept external controls with treatment 1
